title: Assignment
description: An assignment definition stored in assignments/<id>.yml within a PXL Classroom control repository.

allOf.$comment: Open enrollment removes the roster gate, leaving max_acceptances as the only limit on who can claim a repo. It is therefore mandatory whenever roster_mode is open.

id.description: URL-safe slug uniquely identifying the assignment.

description.description: Optional longer description of the assignment.

organization.description: GitHub organization that owns this assignment.

template.description: Source template repository used to create student repos.

owner.description: Owner (user or org) of the template repository.

repository_id.description: Immutable GitHub repository ID of the template. Set once on first use.

assignment_type.description: Whether this is an individual student assignment or a group assignment.

group_config.description: Configuration for group assignments when assignment_type is 'group'.

max_team_size.description: Maximum number of students per team.

min_team_size.description: Target minimum number of students per team (warns on dashboard if under-capacity).

formation_mode.description: How teams are formed: self-service (students pick/create) or pre-assigned (from roster).

allow_team_creation.description: Whether students are allowed to create new teams in self-service mode.

team_name_prefix.description: Optional prefix automatically added to new team names.

unassigned_fallback.description: Only meaningful when formation_mode is 'pre-assigned'. 'block' (default) rejects a student who has no assigned team; 'self-service' lets them join or create a team instead, so late enrollers are not stuck waiting for the lecturer.

repository_name_pattern.description: Naming pattern for repositories. Must contain {github_login} for individual or {team_slug} for group.

opens_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time when the assignment opens for acceptance.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used for display and scheduling. Defaults to Europe/Brussels.

submission_ref.description: Git ref considered as the submission branch.

submission_marker.description: How a student marks the commit that hands the work in, for a template-owned grading workflow that runs on that commit only (`if: github.event.head_commit.message == '...'`). Read when scores are read, by the Admin Panel and by `pxl-classroom grade`; it does not change what is preserved, what is late, or what counts as a submission. Absent means every push grades, which is the ordinary GitHub Classroom workflow.

type.description: What carries the marker. Only `commit_message` today.

value.description: The literal the workflow compares against, e.g. `einde examen`. Matched exactly and case-sensitively on the whole commit message, because that is what the workflow's `==` does.

multiple.description: May a student hand in more than once? `true` (the default, and what an absent field means) grades the LAST hand-in on or before that student's deadline, so a student who spots a mistake and hands in again is graded on the fix. `false` grades the FIRST one: once they have handed in, a later one does not replace it. Either way a hand-in after the deadline is never graded.

student_permission.description: Permission level granted to the student on their repository.

acceptance_mode.description: How student repos are created. Only self-service is implemented: the student opens their invitation link and the repository is provisioned on acceptance. A pre-provisioned mode (lecturer creates repos up front, GitHub sends its own repository invitations) was offered here but implemented nowhere, so selecting it silently produced self-service behaviour.

require_claim.description: Under roster_mode 'open' only: ask each student to confirm an institutional email address, and REFUSE acceptance without one. Default false, so an open assignment stays anonymous unless the lecturer opts in - that is what 'open' is for, and an exam cohort should not be made to identify itself by accident. Under 'claim' an address is inherently required and this flag is not read; under 'enforced' the roster gates by GitHub username and no address is collected. What is required is an ADDRESS, not a roster match: 'open' means anyone with the link may accept, and requiring the address to be on the roster would just be 'claim' by another name. The domain is recorded (`domain_allowed`) rather than enforced, as it already is under open - refusing on domain would lock out a student whose GitHub account carries no institutional address, which is a gate nobody asked for. See lib/claim.mjs.

cohort.description: The students this assignment is for, chosen from the org-wide roster when it was created. Each entry names a roster row: `num:<student_number>` where there is one, `login:<github_login>` for a row promoted from an acceptance, which has no number. Matching accepts EITHER identity a row carries, so a promoted row that later gains a student number through a CSV import still resolves - see lib/cohort.mjs. ABSENT OR EMPTY MEANS EVERY STUDENT ON THE ROSTER, which is what every assignment written before this field means and what an untouched picker means; the form says so on screen, because unticking everything must not silently open an assignment to the whole course. It is a SNAPSHOT: a student added to the roster afterwards is not in it until someone adds them, so the cohort is a record of who the assignment was for rather than a rule that re-evaluates. Only consulted where the roster is the gate (roster_mode 'enforced' or 'claim'); under 'open' the roster does not decide who may accept, so a cohort there would be a control that decides nothing.

cohort_groups.description: The class groups the cohort was selected from. A LABEL, NEVER A GATE - no code path reads this to decide an acceptance, and lib/cohort.mjs does not look at it. It exists so the dashboard card and the detail header can say '3A' instead of leaving a cohort of 22 out of a roster of 40 unexplained. It can go stale: a student who moves to another group afterwards does not change it, which is why the copy beside it names it as how the list was made and not as who is in it.

roster_mode.description: Who may accept. 'enforced' (default) requires the student's login in students/roster.yml. 'claim' is enforced with a way in: the student proves an institutional email address, which must match a roster entry - for the ordinary case where a lecturer holds addresses and not GitHub usernames. 'open' allows any GitHub account within the opens_at..deadline_at window and below max_acceptances; the lecturer reconciles logins to students afterward. A fourth mode, 'org_member', gated on an ACTIVE organization membership so GitHub performed the email-to-account binding; it was withdrawn without ever being used on a cohort, because binding a student to an address should not require putting them in the organization.

claim_domains.$comment: ABSENT and EMPTY are different answers. Omit the field to get the deployment default (CLAIM_DEFAULT_DOMAINS in lib/claim.mjs, shipped here as student.pxl.be and pxl.be); set it to [] to deliberately opt out of any domain restriction. A truthy check would turn that opt-out back into the default.
claim_domains.description: Email domains a claimed address may belong to, matched on the whole domain label and case-insensitively - never as a suffix, since anyone can register notstudent.pxl.be. Omit for the deployment default; set to [] for no restriction. Under 'claim' the roster match is the real gate and this is a cheap early filter; the honest limit is that nothing checks the address EXISTS, so it buys detection and one-address-one-repo accounting rather than prevention.

late_policy.description: What happens on late submissions: report only, or block pushes.

max_acceptances.description: Optional guardrail limiting the number of accepted students.

lock_down_enabled.description: Whether to lock down student repos after the deadline.

feedback_pr.description: If true, provisioning creates a frozen baseline branch and protects it. Lecturers open a draft PR via the CLI/UI to leave inline review comments on student work.

feedback_pr_baseline_branch.description: Name of the frozen baseline branch used as the PR base. Rarely changed.

autograde.description: Optional autograder configuration. Tests can be executed on the lecturer's machine or on GitHub Actions.

enabled.description: Whether autograding is configured for this assignment.

visibility.description: If 'private' and execution_environment is github_actions, uses a reusable workflow to hide tests in the control repo.

type.description: Test taxonomy. `run` executes a shell command; `io` runs a command with stdin and compares stdout; `python` runs a Python script.

command.description: Shell command for type=run, or executable+args for type=io.

script.description: Python source for type=python. Required there, and the only field a python test reads: the CLI runners and the generated Actions workflow all write it to a file and run it, so `command` is ignored.

expected_stdout.description: Expected stdout for type=io. Compared after trim+normalize-newlines.

invite_token.description: Signed invitation token minted at publish time. The broker verifies it before any credential is in scope. PRIVATE - never publish to Pages output.

invite_nonce.description: Invitation generation. Mirrored to the broker INVITE_NONCE variable; rotating it retires every link issued before it.

invite_expires_at.description: Expiry embedded in invite_token. Recorded so republishing reproduces the same token instead of minting a new link.

invite_key.description: PRIVATE half of the acceptance keypair (ECDSA P-256, PKCS#8, base64url), minted at publish time. This is the link secret: the student's browser signs a fresh assertion naming their own GitHub id, so the public acceptance event carries a signature rather than a reusable credential. Never publish to Pages output.

invite_pubkey.description: PUBLIC half of the acceptance keypair (SPKI, base64url), mirrored to the broker's INVITE_PUBKEY variable. Public by design. Its presence is what switches an assignment from the legacy token to signed acceptance.
